notes: Corrected: the head of the נִרְדָּם unit moves from *sleep* to *deep*. Rule 31 resolves this tie by the ASV's own use of the English noun and names תַּרְדֵּמָה → *deep sleep* as a phrase whose noun is the supplied generic and whose modifier is the head; the cognate רָדַם is the same case, so *deep* carries the lexeme. The competing reading, heading on *sleep*, is named in the unit's note under rule 8.

Everything else stands: בַּלָּאט fuses to the single adverb *softly*, headed on the noun, with its assimilated article unrepresented because the one English word carries nothing of the determination (rules 30, 40, 29).
The supplied *a* of *a tent pin* goes to יְתַד, the noun of the expression rather than its leftmost word, and the phrase's article is unrepresented for want of a written *the* (rules 15, 29).
